title: Disentangling Language Effects on Tool Admission and Post-Retrieval Safety
abstract: arXiv:2610.23093v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents increasingly use retrieval tools across languages, yet their safety evaluation remains English-centric. It remains unclear whether language affects tool admission, post-retrieval generation, or both. We independently vary request, retrieved-page, and required response languages in a controlled URL-retrieval setting across ten models and seven languages. We identify Safety Loss through Interlingual Processing (SLIP). Non-English harmful requests increase mean tool admission from 46.9% to 67.4%, with a positive mean change in every model. This pattern also persists in an autonomous retrieval setup across all four models tested in this setting. Requiring answers in the page language increases pooled harmfulness on matched tool calls from 50.3% to 57.4% across four closed-weight models, mainly in Chinese and Hindi. Translating pages alone produces no consistent harm increase in eight models with comparable inference settings. Auto

translated_title: 解耦语言对工具准入与检索后安全性的影响
translated_abstract: 大语言模型智能体越来越多地在多语言环境中使用检索工具，但其安全评估仍然以英语为中心。目前尚不清楚语言究竟影响工具准入、检索后生成，还是两者兼有。我们在受控的URL检索设置中，对十个模型和七种语言独立改变请求语言、检索页面语言和所需回答语言，识别出一种称为“跨语言处理中的安全损失”（SLIP）的现象。非英语有害请求使平均工具准入率从46.9%提升至67.4%，且所有模型的平均变化均为正向。该模式在自主检索设置中对所测试的全部四个模型同样成立。在四个闭源权重模型中，要求以页面语言回答使得匹配工具调用的总体危害性从50.3%上升至57.4%，主要体现在中文和印地语上。而在推理设置相当的八个模型中，仅对页面进行翻译并不会产生一致的危害增加。
tldr: 该研究通过独立控制请求、检索页面和回答语言的受控实验，首次识别出“跨语言处理中的安全损失”（SLIP）现象——非英语有害请求使工具准入率从46.9%升至67.4%，且要求以页面语言回答会进一步增加危害性，从而将语言对LLM智能体工具准入与检索后安全的影响分离出来。
en_tdlr: This paper disentangles language effects on tool admission and post-retrieval safety in LLM agents by independently varying request, page, and response languages, identifying Safety Loss through Interlingual Processing (SLIP) where non-English harmful requests raise tool admission from 46.9% to 67.4%, while requiring answers in the page language further increases harmfulness.
